exposure: Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block with 20 mL of 0.25% ropivacaine
Wound-site infiltration (WSI) with 20 mL of 0.25% ropivacaine
outcome: Time to first rescue analgesia demand
Total number of parturients needing second rescue pain management in 24 hours
Sequelae correlated to TAP block and infiltration method
cohort: The study included 60 parturients posted for elective surgical delivery under subarachnoid block.
finding: The Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block with 0.25% ropivacaine provided superior postoperative analgesia and significantly delayed the time to first rescue analgesia compared to wound-site infiltration (WSI) in patients undergoing cesarean delivery.
